class.name: PhysXWaterSurface3D
class.brief_description: A real animated water surface: a GPU FFT ocean spectrum layer plus a local ripple layer that bodies can disturb, rendered as a displaced mesh.
class.description: Two coupled simulation layers, both real-time GPU compute through the shared main [RenderingDevice] when windowed: a local iWave-style ripple layer (a damped 2D wave equation you can disturb via [method submit_sphere]/[method submit_impulse]) and a Tessendorf FFT ocean spectrum layer (large-scale wind-driven chop, tuned by [member wind_speed]/[member wind_direction]/[member wave_amplitude]). Rendering also produces optional light-space caustics with a direct [RenderingDevice] graphics pass; it does not create a second [SubViewport]. A child [MeshInstance3D] (a subdivided [PlaneMesh], sized to [member ocean_domain_size], or the resampled [member surface_mesh] footprint) is created automatically and displaced by both layers, summed. Call [method sample_height] to query the same combined surface on the CPU -- e.g. from a buoyancy script (see [code]demo/common/buoyant_body.gd[/code] in the paired demo project) -- and [method submit_sphere] once per physics tick per floating body so it actually disturbs the ripple layer, not just receives a height back. No [RenderingDevice] compute support (e.g. running headless) leaves the surface flat and [method sample_height] returning [member water_level] plus zero -- a graceful no-op, not an error, matching every other GPU solver in this module. Set [member surface_mesh] to give the water any outline -- a round pool, a kidney-bean pond, a lake with an island. Waves reflect off its shoreline, and [method sample_height]/[method is_wet] report no water outside it. Both simulation grids are centred on the node's global position (plus the [member surface_mesh] footprint's centre), fixed when the node enters the tree or a property changes. The node's rotation and scale are not applied to the simulation, so keep it unrotated and unscaled. Only runs in an actual running game, never in the editor -- placing or moving the node in the Inspector does not simulate.

method.name: get_caustics_texture
method.description: The zero-copy caustics light-pattern texture. Project a receiving surface's world position onto [method get_caustics_light_right] and [method get_caustics_light_up], relative to [method get_caustics_origin], and map the result through [method get_caustics_half_extent] to sample the texture. Null until [member caustics_enabled] is true and the node has built.

method.name: get_caustics_half_extent
method.description: Half-width of the square light-space projection in world units, used to map receiver positions to [method get_caustics_texture] UV coordinates.

method.name: get_caustics_light_right
method.description: Light-space horizontal projection axis used to sample [method get_caustics_texture].

method.name: get_caustics_light_up
method.description: Light-space vertical projection axis used to sample [method get_caustics_texture].

method.name: get_caustics_origin
method.description: World-space center of the light-space caustics projection.

method.name: clear_sphere
method.description: Removes a previously-submitted sphere proxy (see [method submit_sphere]) by its owner id. Call this when a floating body leaves the water or is freed; a proxy left in place otherwise keeps disturbing the ripple layer at its last submitted position.

method.name: is_wet
method.description: Whether [code]world_pos[/code]'s XZ lies inside the [member surface_mesh] footprint, at the ripple grid's resolution. Always [code]true[/code] when no [member surface_mesh] is set. [code]world_pos.y[/code] is ignored.

method.name: sample_height
method.description: The combined surface height (ripple + ocean layers, plus [member water_level]) at [code]world_pos[/code]'s XZ, bilinearly sampled from the last periodic readback (a few frames behind the GPU simulation -- fine for buoyancy, not meant for sub-frame precision). [code]world_pos.y[/code] is ignored. Returns [code]-INF[/code] where [method is_wet] is [code]false[/code] (outside the [member surface_mesh] footprint), so anything comparing a point's height against it -- a buoyancy script's submersion depth -- reads "not in water" there.

method.name: submit_impulse
method.description: A one-shot local disturbance (a splash) at [code]world_pos[/code]'s XZ -- consumed by the next simulation step, then cleared automatically. Call it once per event (e.g. on impact), not every tick.

method.name: submit_sphere
method.description: A persistent body proxy that pushes the ripple layer's surface down near [code]world_pos[/code]'s XZ, proportional to [code]radius[/code] and [code]strength[/code]. Call once per physics tick while a body is in the water (e.g. from its own [code]_physics_process[/code]), keyed by any id stable for that body's lifetime -- [code]get_instance_id()[/code] works well. Call [method clear_sphere] with the same id when the body leaves.

members.member: Approximate distance the refracted light travels below the surface before it is mapped into the caustics texture. Larger values spread the pattern farther sideways for oblique light.
Enables the light-space caustics draw pass and its render target. When disabled, the extra GPU buffers and draw are skipped. See [method get_caustics_texture].
World-space direction that light travels from the source toward the water. It need not be normalized.
Damping (ALPHA) on the local ripple layer's wave equation -- higher settles disturbances faster.

Water depth used by the ripple wave equation and FFT ocean dispersion relation. Shallower water reduces ripple propagation speed and changes ocean-wave timing; it does not directly reduce wave height.

World-space extent (X, Z) of the local ripple layer -- independent of [member ocean_domain_size], see [member ocean_grid_resolution]'s own note on why. Ignored when [member surface_mesh] is set: the ripple grid is then fitted to the footprint's bounds.
Cell count per side of the local ripple layer's grid. Not required to be a power of two, unlike [member ocean_grid_resolution].
World-space extent (X, Z) of the FFT ocean layer -- also the size of the rendered [PlaneMesh].

Cell count per side of the FFT ocean layer's grid. Rounded up to the nearest power of two if set otherwise -- the Stockham FFT passes require it. Independent of [member grid_resolution]/[member domain_size] (the ripple layer's own grid) by design: they're two different consumers of "water height" with very different resolution/precision needs, kept architecturally separate rather than forced to share one grid.
Multiplier on the ripple displacement driven by submitted floating-body proxies and impulses. Set lower for small splashes and wakes in a pool; this does not scale the FFT ocean waves.

Optional water outline: any flat [Mesh] (node-local) whose up-facing triangles' X/Z footprint is the water -- e.g. a disc baked from a [CSGCylinder3D], or a shape modelled elsewhere. Its own vertices are not displaced directly; the footprint is resampled into an even grid clipped to the outline, so a coarse or fan-triangulated mesh still gets vertices to animate everywhere. When set, the ripple grid is fitted to the footprint's bounds ([member domain_size] is ignored) at [member grid_resolution], cells outside it are dry land the waves reflect off, caustics are cut to the water area, and [method sample_height] returns [code]-INF[/code] over dry cells. The FFT ocean layer still covers [member ocean_domain_size] around the same centre -- size it to cover the footprint. Unset, the water is the square [member domain_size] / [member ocean_domain_size] plane.
Mean world-space Y of the surface -- place the node here rather than relying on its own transform, since the rendered mesh and both simulation layers are displaced relative to this baseline.

The material driving the surface mesh's displacement/shading. A default is created automatically if left unset -- assign your own only if you need to customize the look; it must keep sampling [code]ripple_height_tex[/code]/[code]ocean_height_tex[/code] in its vertex shader the same way the default does, or the mesh will stop moving.
Linear height multiplier for the FFT ocean waves. Values below 1 reduce wave height proportionally; 0 removes the FFT ocean waves. This does not scale local ripple disturbances.
Wind direction (X, Z) driving the FFT ocean layer's wave alignment. Need not be normalized.
Wind speed driving the FFT ocean layer's spectrum -- higher produces longer, larger waves.
